draft.title: Substituting into formulas
card: A letter in a formula is a variable. It stands for a number that can change. To substitute, give each letter one value and write the numbers in brackets if they could be confused with signs.
Then work it out in the usual order: brackets first, then powers, then \(\times\) and \(\div\) from left to right, then \(+\) and \(-\) from left to right.
Example: speed \(s = d \div t\). For \(d = 150\) and \(t = 3\), \(s = 150 \div 3 = 50\).

Example: \(A = \frac{1}{2}bh\) with \(b = 6\) and \(h = 4\). \(A = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 3 \times 4 = 12\). Another: \(P = 2l + 2w\) with \(l = 5\) and \(w = 3\) gives \(P = 10 + 6 = 16\), because the \(\times\) is done before the \(+\).
draft.remember: Replace each letter with its number, then follow the order of operations.

a.q: A fence has a perimeter given by \(P = 2l + 2w\). Find \(P\) when \(l = 7\) and \(w = 4\).
a.why: \(P = 2 \times 7 + 2 \times 4 = 14 + 8 = 22\). The answer 64 comes from working strictly left to right: \(2 \times 7 = 14\), then \(14 + 2 = 16\), then \(16 \times 4 = 64\), which does the \(+\) before the second \(\times\). The answer 18 comes from forgetting to double \(w\), giving \(14 + 4\).
a.clue: Do each multiplication before the addition.

b.q: Dana rides 36 km in 3 hours. Use \(s = d \div t\) with \(d = 36\) and \(t = 3\). What is her speed in km/h?
b.why: \(s = 36 \div 3 = 12\) km/h. The answer 108 comes from multiplying \(d\) and \(t\) instead of dividing. The answers 39 and 33 come from adding or subtracting the two numbers.
b.clue: Distance goes on top, time goes underneath.

proposal.title: Variables and substitution
card: A letter in a formula is a variable. It stands for a number that can change. To substitute, replace each letter with its value. A number next to a letter means multiply, so \(2l\) means \(2 \times l\).
Then work it out in the usual order: brackets first, then powers, then \(\times\) and \(\div\) from left to right, then \(+\) and \(-\) from left to right.
Example: speed \(s = d \div t\). For \(d = 150\) and \(t = 3\), \(s = 150 \div 3 = 50\).
Example: \(P = 2l + 2w\) with \(l = 5\) and \(w = 3\). \(P = 2 \times 5 + 2 \times 3\), which is \(10 + 6 = 16\), because each \(\times\) is done before the \(+\).
proposal.remember: Replace each letter with its number, then follow the order of operations.

a.q: A fence has a perimeter given by \(P = 2l + 2w\). Find \(P\) when \(l = 7\) and \(w = 4\).
a.why: \(P = 2 \times 7 + 2 \times 4\), which is \(14 + 8 = 22\). The answer 64 comes from working strictly left to right: \(14 + 2 = 16\), then \(16 \times 4 = 64\), which does the \(+\) before the second \(\times\). The answer 18 comes from forgetting to double \(w\), and 51 from reading \(2l\) as 27 instead of \(2 \times 7\).
a.clue: Do each multiplication before the addition.
